root_cause.defect: opintel_intelligence_worker/coordinator_persistence.py _migrate_repair_attempt_lineage() treats the presence of the repair_attempt_lineage_sha256 column as proof that the whole attempt-scoped identity migration completed: `columns = {...}; if "repair_attempt_lineage_sha256" in columns: return`. The composite-uniqueness rescoping (DROP legacy single-column uq_m67_coordinator_release / uq_m67_coordinator_work_item, ADD UNIQUE(column, repair_attempt_lineage_sha256)) sits AFTER that early return, inside the same guard.
root_cause.how_production_reached_a_partial_state: The final Repair #4 image d1b7a04 (deployed digest sha256:751e410f...) added the composite-constraint rescoping. But a superseded Repair #4 iteration (image sha256:3065292651..., commit 6bb8b346) had already run an earlier _migrate_ that added the repair_attempt_lineage_sha256 column WITHOUT the rescoping (that iteration then failed at exactly this same UniqueViolation, which is what d1b7a04 was built to fix). When d1b7a04 first ran initialize(), the column already existed, so _migrate_ returned early and the rescoping never executed against production.
